picture:talk.src.svg.answer: A chat window titled 'Ogmios' where the user talks with an AI conversation partner in English, with the labels 'No corrections now. Just talk.' and 'Stuck? Ask how to say it.' The user's message about finishing a big report is already sent, and the partner has replied with a question about how the team reacted. The reply box holds 'Honestly, I did a big effort, but in the end it worked' with a '12 of about 40 words' counter. The cursor moves to the microphone button and turns into a hand to press it. A waveform pill appears above the button while it records, then goes away and a ring shows around the mic. Next the partner's message gets a purple outline, the mic ring stays on, and the cursor waits near the input. The final frame shows the outlined partner message, the waveform pill, the ringed mic button and a 'How do I say...?' chip.
picture:talk.src.svg.why: Chat with an AI partner, No corrections now, mic and reply box: talk by voice or typing, no corrections mid-conversation.

section:Talk, and nobody stops you.answer: You choose a topic and a level (basic to advanced), then speak by holding the microphone or type. An AI partner asks questions and follows the conversation without correcting you. A "How do I say…?" button suggests English phrasings from your own language. Speech is turned into text on your computer, and you can edit that text before sending it.
section:Talk, and nobody stops you.why: The reader understood the section as its claim, in substance.

picture:improve.src.svg.answer: The stages a mistake goes through as it is learned: Detected, In focus, Improving, Mastered, set on a timeline that runs left to right. Four cards sit in a row: 'Detected / In your report' with 'I did a big effort' struck out, 'In focus / Your partner steers to it' with placeholder bars, 'Improving / A two-minute drill' with 'made an effort', and 'Mastered / Right in a real talk' with 'I made a big effort'. A pink dot moves along the dashed line below them, and each card lights up as the dot reaches it. At the end a check mark appears on Mastered. The final frame shows all four cards lit, the first two pink and the last two green.
picture:improve.src.svg.why: Mistake moves Detected, In focus, Improving, Mastered with Mastered as right in a real talk.

section:How it helps you improve.answer: After a conversation you get what went well, one main thing to work on and at most two smaller points. For grammar, you try to fix your own sentence first. Repeated mistakes become patterns that move through detected, in focus, improving and mastered. Later conversations steer you toward them, optional two-minute drills exist, and a pattern counts as mastered only when you get it right in real conversation.
section:How it helps you improve.why: The reader understood the section as its claim, in substance.

picture:books.src.svg.answer: Reading a book file ('alice.epub'): a chart of which chapters you can read, plus a vocabulary card for a word taken from the book with a review schedule. A book icon labelled alice.epub points to a 'Chapters you can read' bar chart where the first three bars are full and green and the rest are shorter and blue. A pink highlight passes over the fourth bar, which then becomes full and green. Beside it, a card for 'curtsey' shows the sentence 'She tried to curtsey as she spoke', then 'Into your language and back' with a check mark that appears. Under 'Back after' the day buttons 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 light up one after another. The final frame shows four green chapters with the fourth highlighted, the checked card and all five day buttons outlined.
picture:books.src.svg.why: Book file to chapters-you-can-read chart, word card with the book sentence, review at 1/3/7/21/60 days.

section:Learn the words of your own book.answer: You add an English EPUB or PDF and Ogmios prepares it chapter by chapter. A bar per chapter fills as you learn its words, and a full bar means the chapter is ready to read. Each word is practised with a sentence from the book, translated into your language and back. You can skip words you already know. Words come back after 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days and the partner uses them in conversation. A chapter can also be translated sentence by sentence, used to practise sentence structures, or used for dictations.
section:Learn the words of your own book.why: The reader understood the section as its claim, in substance.

picture:privacy.src.svg.answer: Privacy and data flow: voice and data stay on 'Your computer', and only text goes out to 'Claude'. Inside a box labelled 'Your computer' with a lock, a 'Your voice' waveform is turned into the text 'Honestly, I did a big effort,' under 'Turned into text'. A small green square moves from that text through the box's edge along a dashed arrow toward the 'Claude' box, which lights up. A purple square then comes back into the computer box, and a purple reply bubble 'How did your team react?' appears. 'Books and progress' with progress bars stays inside the computer box the whole time. The final frame shows the full flow with 'Only text goes out' under Claude.
picture:privacy.src.svg.why: Voice, books and progress stay inside Your computer; only text goes out to Claude.

section:Your data stays on your computer.answer: Conversations, recordings, books and progress are saved locally and there is no Ogmios account. Speech recognition runs on your machine, so your voice never leaves it. Claude receives only the text of your conversations and, when you prepare a chapter, the text of that chapter.
section:Your data stays on your computer.why: The reader understood the section as its claim, in substance.

readme.answer: Ogmios is a free desktop app for macOS and Windows that lets English learners practise speaking with Claude without being interrupted, then gives them one focused correction in their native language, tracks their repeated mistakes until they are mastered in conversation, and teaches the vocabulary of English books they want to read.
readme.why: Reader summary matches: speak with Claude uninterrupted, one focused correction, book vocabulary.
